questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had an academic interest in German literature, film and philosophy, as well as an immense interest in Berlin theatre. I also wanted to improve my German.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite simple. everything was informed to me on e-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found a place to stay through my host university, they also offered orientation days and a German pre-course, that I attended.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student dorms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchens.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: it's far away from Berlin centre, so it can feel a bit isolationg in the student dorms, unless one is mostly here to chat with other exchange students. but it is close to the uni.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to attend one of the first two seminars as well as sign up on a campus website. We could drop a course anytime.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had an introduction lecture in the orientation days, where the course process was walked through. very helpful. I didn't require further assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To attend the introductory lectures during the orientation days.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did courses specifically for exchange students (international courses). the level fit me well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: at my home university I have fewer courses, but courses that require more time and effort, and with more difficult exams. here I had many different courses that all required less effort. the language required more effort here, of course, so the courses were a bit less ambitious than what I've experienced at my home university, but I would say that that was fitting, when the courses were targeted exchange students. my courses here required more active participation during seminars and a lot of physical attendance (something like 80%) which is different to my home university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
course 16901: Berlin im Film
Course 16915: Creative Walking
Course 16917: Visions and Images of the city and the Metropolis in theory, reality and fiction.
Course 16922: Reading Hitler
Course 16916: Literary legacy of nuclear disaster

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
My favorite of the courses I listed were Visions and Images of the city and the metropolis. the course provides an immensely interesting theoretical and creative background to the city, especially the city of berlin. it was very enlightening and inspiring.
I also enjoyed Literary legacy of nuclear disaster, as we read German literature that I normally would never get the chance to read, and its a topic that has been quite important for German politics and history.
I also recommend the course berlin im film, as it provides such a fantastic background for moving around berlin, as well as an immersion into berlin history throughout the 20th and start 21st century.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: there's a semester fee in the beginning of the semester, but this includes transportation in all of Berlin.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is generally less expensive than Copenhagen, so I didn't struggle too much. housing can be expensive though, is One lives off campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different sports, parties and excursions were available. I did dance twice a week, which was great. I also went to art museums with my uni.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend signing up for a sport. its good quality teaching, and a nice break form academic pursuits.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to the theatre as much as possible. it's some of the greatest theatre I've seen. there's also so many great cafes and bars in berlin as well as art exhibitions.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was pretty easy. its not too far from danish culture, and I had a few friends here already.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I recommend doing courses with local students. I didn't and so I haven't met any. I also recommend moving into a WG with German students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: you have a more formal relationship to professors here. you also have to attend almost all of your classes and participate actively.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: teatre, film, literature, music here is all amazing. also some very beautiful/interesting architecture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Try and find a place near the city. it's difficult to experience the magic of the city very often, when you're far away. 2. go to cultural experiences as often as possible, let it also inspire you're academic pursuits. 3. go walk aimlessly around your city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try not to be too academically insecure. it's really intimidating to be an exchange student, and there are formalities that youre not familiar with. However, as long as you try your best, there is no reason to stress. you're teachers will understand, that you're not a native.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Cultural and social experiences here. meeting some great people and doing fun things together, like eating out or go to a concert. also some really inspiring courses at uni. learning more about German history was so interesting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I wasn't satisfied with my living conditions. it was about an hour from City Centre, and it was difficult for me to take that trip so often, and sometimes late in the evening. of you want to explore the city a lot, I recommend finding something outside of the uni.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
